messages:
maya: Heads up — after the autotuner rollout last night we're seeing a tail-latency regression for long sequences on A100 pools. p99 up ~3-5% for seqlen >=512 :eyes:

ravi: Which model/route and any profiler output?

maya: model redwood/encoder-6b@2026-03-10, route /generate-stream. Quick profiler snippet:
```
A100 sm80 profile:
- seqlen 128 -> fused_attn_v3 (chosen)
- seqlen 256 -> fused_attn_v3
- seqlen 512 -> unfused_attn (fallback) -> ~12% slower
- seqlen 1024 -> unfused_attn, big KV-copy overhead
KV hit rate dropped 87% -> 61% for these cases
```

eli: Two quick hypotheses:
1) autotuner prioritized median latency over tail for recent windows so chose cheaper per-token kernels with worse tail under contention.
2) KV keying/persistence mismatch — keys rotate on driver or kernel changes causing cold misses.

zach: We did add kernel_digest into some cache keys in the selector refactor — might explain invalidation across versions.

maya: Yep. The autotuner change added `kernel_digest` to the autotune cache id but it leaked into the prefix-KV key builder via a refactor.

ravi: Paste the key format being used.

maya: Current simplified key format:
```
model:{model_id}:ver:{ver}:driver:{driver_id}:kernel:{kernel_digest}:kv:{sha1(prefix)}
```
This was meant for autotune store only but ended up used for user prefix KV.

eli: That would cause persistent cold misses when driver_id or kernel_digest change. We should never include ephemeral fields in user KV keys.

ops-bot: Deploy auditor: autotuner v2.4 rolled to eng-runtime A100 pool 2026-03-16T03:12Z (100%) :white_check_mark:

zach: Also found a seqlen binning bug — boundary for 512 was exclusive, so some 512 requests hit the wrong kernel path. Tiny comparator bug, will PR.

ml-bot: Auto-profile alert job=2026-03-16_04:00 — p99 tokens/sec dropped 3.8% for seqlen>=512 on A100 sm80. Likely causes: kernel pick change + KV cold misses.

ravi: Action items:
- remove kernel_digest and driver_id from user KV keys (maya)
- add migration/compat fallback for existing keys for 48h (eli)
- revert autotuner metric weighting to penalize tail (zach)
- unit test for seqlen bin boundaries (zach)

maya: I'll split key builders (autotune-store vs prefix-KV) and add a compatibility read path: try digest-key -> fallback legacy-key. Also will avoid writing driver_id/kernel_digest into user namespace.

eli: Persistence plan: keep both namespaces for 48h. Read: try digest-key -> legacy -> populate legacy on success. Stagger TTLs to avoid mass repop.

zach: Autotuner change: switch scoring to 95th percentile latency (instead of median) + cost-per-token penalty to avoid high-variance high-throughput picks. Also add concurrency-aware microbenchmarks.

maya: Quick mitigation: runtime flag to force kernel-group mapping to previous stable variant on affected routes, toggled via console.

ravi: Add dashboard panel for KV-hit-rate broken down by key-namespace and driver_id so we can detect namespace inflation.

maya: Canary plan: apply key-split + seqlen-fix on 20% of A100 pool tomorrow morning and monitor p99 and KV-hit-rate.

zach: PRs: seqlen-bin-fix #4721, key-builder-split #4722, autotuner-score-adjust #4723

ops-bot: Canary started autotuner-fix 20% of A100 pool at 2026-03-16T12:10Z.

maya: Will follow up after canary. If p99 >2% regression persists we will rollback autotuner. :warning:

eli: Note: on SM90 quantized nodes KV-copy cost under concurrency is higher. Include concurrency ramps in autotuner harness (batch size + inflight tokens).

zach: Adding synthetic concurrency ramps to the autotuner benchmarks.

ravi: Assign owners and set 24h on-call rotation until stable: @maya (kv/key), @zach (kernel selector), @eli (autotuner scoring).

maya: Added owners and infra ticket with test plan. Will post canary results.
